name: Interiors & More Limited
sector: Artificial flowers and event/home-decor manufacturing and distribution
summary: Interiors & More manufactures and trades artificial flowers, plants and event/home-decor products, using local production, stocked assortment and regional outlets to compete with imported supply. Its sales expansion is genuine: standalone revenue rose from INR 24.86 crore in FY2023 to INR 79.49 crore in FY2026. But the economic question has moved from demand to cash: consolidated inventory is INR 61.43 crore, debt INR 56.35 crore, and three-year operating cash conversion remains negative even after relocating plant advances out of operating cash flow. This is a manufacturing-and-distribution scale-up, not an evidence-backed compounder. At the last observed INR 133 trade on October 13, the funded central model earns 8.99% annually over five years versus a 15% hurdle. BQS 5.1, GQS 5.0 after the persistent-cash cap, and IAS 3.4 indicate a weak assessed setup/value-trap risk, not a claim of misconduct. Better collection/inventory evidence, financed completion and a lower entry price could change that conclusion. [S1–S6,S11]

Eligible SME series and 35 recorded trades/sessions across 60 days, but extreme theoretical exit length and stale quote. No suspension claim; live executability unresolved.

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: Interiors & More manufactures and trades artificial flowers, plants and event/home-decor products, using local production, stocked assortment and regional outlets to compete with imported supply. Its sales expansion is genuine: standalone revenue rose from INR 24.86 crore in FY2023 to INR 79.49 crore in FY2026. But the economic question has moved from demand to cash: consolidated inventory is INR 61.43 crore, debt INR 56.35 crore, and three-year operating cash conversion remains negative even after relocating plant advances out of operating cash flow. This is a manufacturing-and-distribution scale-up, not an evidence-backed compounder. At the last observed INR 133 trade on October 13, the funded central model earns 8.99% annually over five years versus a 15% hurdle. BQS 5.1, GQS 5.0 after the persistent-cash cap, and IAS 3.4 indicate a weak assessed setup/value-trap risk, not a claim of misconduct. Better collection/inventory evidence, financed completion and a lower entry price could change that conclusion. [S1–S6,S11]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Cutoff: October 20, 2026; last market session October 19. Full legal identity: Interiors & More Limited, NSE SME INM, ISIN INE0OPC01015. Incorporation date in the prospectus is July 30, 2012; the annual note contains a different legacy wording, so identity follows the consistent legal/security identifiers rather than that sentence. Consolidated Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards accounts are used, with the Dubai company wholly owned and INM House struck off March 23, 2026. No minority claim is identified. Financial stocks are March 31, 2026, not an invented October balance sheet. Current issued shares are 13,990,800 after the December 5, 2025 1:1 bonus; September warrants are additional contingent claims. The quote is INR 133 from October 13, four sessions before October 19, and supports only a dated conditional price assessment. Market capitalization is INR 186.08 crore. Horizon ends October 13, 2031; equity hurdle 15% nominal before personal tax; illustrative liquidity position INR 5 lakh, not a recommended allocation. Historical facts, governance, growth decomposition, returns and valuation inputs have Medium material confidence because of short comparable post-pandemic history and bounded presentation/operating-definition gaps. Identity and main audited stock/flow values are High confidence; forecasts remain highly uncertain. G1–G4 are Conditional, with no evidenced severe integrity or actual default conclusion. [S1,S3–S8,S11–S15]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS raw/final 5.06, GQS raw 6.05/final 5.00, IAS raw/final 3.415. Coverage is 100% under original weights; no neutral missing score, reweighting or discretionary haircut is used. Factors are GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 4, CASH 3, BAL 4, EXEC 5, EARN 5; IAS uses Q 5.06, R 3, D 3, P 4 and L 1. REV starts in the ≥30% CAGR band 9 but is capped at 8 for Medium confidence and three relevant comparable intervals. CASH 3 triggers only the explicit persistent cash-realization GQS cap 5; the immature-capital caveat prevents a separate assertion of persistent CAP destruction. No governance or funding-failure cap is imposed because audited records do not establish those failures. Every factor's affirmative and contrary evidence is in the factor audit. Display uses half-up one decimal, while classification and IAS retain unrounded numbers. Moving GOV and CAP by one point changes BQS by ±0.32, GQS raw by ±0.15 and IAS via Q by ±0.08; the GQS cap remains 5. Scores are policy heuristics, not empirically validated forecasts. [S1–S6,S11–S15]

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: The assortment covers artificial flowers and greenery, vases, props, decorative lighting, furniture and event materials. Buyers include decorators, wedding/event operators, wholesalers, retail customers and export customers. Manufactured products replace some bought-in/imported products; sales are recognized on dispatch/delivery/customer acceptance as applicable, after inter-branch eliminations. FY2026 group revenue is INR 83.60 crore after INR 39.02 crore of inter-branch sales are removed; gross branch movement is not end-customer revenue. Stock breadth offers immediate availability but ties up cash for long periods. Supplier advances add to this exposure. The Dubai subsidiary broadens geography; its separately audited AED accounts are included in group results. Exports recorded in the group revenue note are INR 2.749 crore; this is not necessarily all overseas subsidiary sales, so the two are not conflated. The June 2025 call's cumulative customer/SKU claims describe management's reach, not contracted recurring revenue or independently verified retention. [S1,S4,S10]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: The credible advantage is operational: a domestic, broad-assortment platform can shorten replenishment/customization times compared with importing finished decor, while local showrooms lower discovery friction. Evidence includes actual local manufacturing, the broad SKU offer and regional openings. Durability is limited by fashion/design changes, substitutable imported products and buyers' ability to source elsewhere. The prospectus disclosed FY2023 top-five customer revenue 43.53% and top-five supplier purchases 59.15%, without long-term agreements. Those are historical observations, not claimed current concentration. FY2026 concentration and repeat-customer cohorts are not available in the reviewed notes. Nilkamal is a furniture/home-retail comparator, Cello a branded manufacturing/distribution comparator, and Archies an assortment-led gifting/decor retailer. None is a clean artificial-flower pure play, and their trading multiples are not imported into this valuation. Independent category market share, a sustainable price premium and customer switching costs remain unproved. MOAT 5 credits useful execution capability without mistaking an attractive product catalog, recognizable buyers or a factory for a structural barrier. [S1,S4,S9,S10,S16–S18]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Primary observations are INR 6.4273,9.8916,24.8566,32.4224,58.8919 and 83.5966 crore for FY2021–FY2026 respectively. The first two are IPO-restated standalone, FY2023 matches the later parent base, and FY2024 onward is consolidated. Annual additions are INR 3.4643,14.9650,7.5658,26.4695 and 24.7047 crore. A five-year endpoint calculation is 67.04%, but starts in a pandemic-distorted year and changes perimeter, so it is context, not the scored window. Standalone FY2023–FY2026 revenue 24.8566→79.4939 gives 47.33%; consolidated 24.8566→83.5966 gives 49.82%. This independently shows growth is not merely adding the Dubai reporting perimeter, though a precise organic volume/price/mix decomposition is ND. FY2026 standalone growth 47.12% and group growth 41.95% remain strong. Expansion of distribution, own production and assortment are management-attributed drivers; no unsupported percentage split is invented. No September 2026 result was available in the reviewed filing interval, and a seasonal half-year is not annualized. Revenue history before FY2021 and a valid 10-year CAGR are ND. The enormous percentage is not penalized simply for starting small; the pandemic/perimeter correction and evidence ceiling are applied once. [S1–S4]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Management describes an approximately 200,000-square-foot owned manufacturing platform, deeper import substitution, export development and branded stores. Its broad five-year revenue capability discussion is INR 150–200 crore, not a funded order book. The base model reaches INR 169.14 crore annualized revenue by October 2031 using 18%,16%,14%,12%,10% and a fractional final 10% growth interval; 25% EBITDA margin does not return to FY2023's 38% peak. Already-paid CWIP and plant advances are commissioned without paying them again, while INR 5–6 crore of annual incremental cash capex is funded. Inventory/receivables/payables drive a reduction in net operating WC/revenue from 92.03% opening to 85%,80%,78%,76% and 75%. This efficiency improvement, and seasonal timing, are assumptions rather than achieved results. The bull case reaches INR 220.61 crore with more fresh capex, 28% later margins and fully paid warrant dilution; it exceeds the conservative capability range and requires additional productivity/distribution success. The raw GQS 6.05 is capped 5 because growing sales have not yet converted into cumulative cash. Access to demand is not enough without a financed stock and plant cycle. [S1,S4–S6,S9,S10]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The founder-led team has built a listed manufacturing/distribution platform and reports 69.47% promoter ownership in the standalone share note. Director remuneration is INR 1.7053 crore, 12.60% of group PAT, versus INR 1.08 crore previously. Personal guarantees and related-party finance support lenders but do not independently establish minority alignment. The consolidated RPT table repeats INR 11.1925 crore loan lines and does not transparently bridge all borrowing movements; the ICS Mobile INR 2.0183 crore closing loan is included in debt regardless of this disclosure gap. There is no evidence here establishing diversion. The statutory opinion is unmodified, with revenue and inventory KAMs and no reported fraud/default/disputed statutory dues. The company explained the May 2026 capital/EPS mismatch as an initial PDF clerical error corrected that day, with XBRL already correct. The secretarial report records three late forms with additional fees INR 2,400, 1,200 and 3,600; management calls them procedural and says monitoring was strengthened. The 2024 prospectus separately disclosed manufacturing before the MOA object amendment and a compounding application then pending. No specific disposal was found, while the FY2026 audit states no pending litigation impacting financial position. This is unresolved historical compliance follow-through, not proof of continuing illegality or a material liability. Promoter personal tax proceedings disclosed historically are not charged to company cash. Execution is mixed: June 2025 plans for 10–20 B2C and 10–15 B2B stores do not have a reconciled delivered cohort; a second Hyderabad franchise did open September 1, 2026. FY2026 molding output 444,376 kg missed 518,546 kg target by 14.30%, attributed in the report to staffing/material constraints. Capacity commentary alternates between roughly half and 95% utilization without a reconciled denominator; neither is used as an audited volume forecast. [S1,S4,S7–S10,S19]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The six-year financial table retains original/restated scope distinctions. For FY2024/FY2025/FY2026, reported PAT is INR 7.0465/11.9696/13.5361 crore; CFO −9.8523/−15.8170/+6.6445; cash PPE/CWIP capex 1.9512/21.8392/27.4823. Cumulative CFO/PAT is -0.584x and total FCF proxy −70.2975 crore. Cash advance for plant was classified in CFO: relocating 3.5218 in FY2025 and 4.6100 in FY2026 makes economic CFO −12.2952/+11.2545 and raises investment identically. The corrected cumulative conversion is still -0.335x. Thus capex classification explains part, but not all, of weak cash realization; this is an analytical reclassification, not missing cash. FY2026 cash reconciles 2.1979+6.6445−27.1468+22.9395≈4.6351 crore after rounding. Inventory rose 12.0455 crore and receivables 2.7839, partly funded by payables 4.8492. Average receivable-days improved 82.1→75.9; average inventory/material-cost days improved 534.3→478.5, but remain extreme. Receivables over one year are 0.6866 crore versus 1.2233 prior; six-to-twelve-month balances rose to 1.9447 crore.

Financial-capital proxy equity+debt−cash−FD is INR 23.8620/44.4440/95.3877/131.5042 crore for FY2023–FY2026; full CWIP and advance funding are retained, including immature capacity. At 25% normalized operating tax, NOPAT 8.9795×75%=6.7346 in FY2023 and 19.4162×75%=14.5622 in FY2026 produce a 7.27% incremental proxy, not project IRR. FY2026 average-capital ROIC proxy is 12.84% versus a 12–15% analytical nominal INR cost-of-capital range.

Every opening claim is assigned once. Ordinary statutory/expense/salary/creditor balances remain in WC; current tax 3.9140, current gratuity 0.0148, capital retention 1.4496 and declared dividend 0.69954 are paid explicitly; term/current debt is counted once. Noncurrent gratuity 0.3500 and DTL 0.3858 remain terminal claims. Deposits are not free cash. The 0.0148 untyped revenue-authority credit is excluded centrally, with a separate recovery sensitivity. The note 9 component sum differs from its printed total, and note 8 line rounding differs by INR 2,000; the face balance and explicit rounding lines are retained. These immaterial presentation differences do not justify a blanket reliability fail. The INR 10 crore printed revolving limit versus INR 22.3459 crore drawn requires clarification; no unused facility headroom is inferred. [S1–S6]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At 133 and 13,990,800 shares, market capitalization is INR 186.0776 crore. Matching March 31 debt/cash gives net debt 51.7099 and enterprise value 237.7875; the cross-checks are P/E 13.75x, EV/EBITDA 11.20x, EV/EBIT 12.25x and P/B 2.33x. These are dated bridges, not observed October cash. The central terminal 8x EBIT multiple normalizes below the current bridge; the bull 10x and adaptive-bear 6x are assumptions, not peer targets.

The central model's terminal EBIT is INR 37.02 crore, cash 15.66, debt 24.91, retained gratuity/DTL 0.7358, equity 286.17 and price 204.54, giving 8.99% annual return. Bull price 370.01 / IRR 22.71% uses 1.55448 crore diluted shares and matching exercise proceeds. Adaptive bear price 45.14 / IRR -19.44% requires stock reduction, capex restraint and continued revolver access; the no-reset bear cannot fund itself. No IRR is assigned to an unfunded negative-cash path.

The received INR 6.95415 crore warrant deposit enters only on September 8; 82% is earmarked for WC and 18% for GCP. INR 20.86245 crore additional cash is optional, not available centrally. Full exercise in the base operating case reduces per-share terminal value to INR 197.51, despite more cash, because dilution is real. The already-declared dividend is a company cash outflow without return credit to this post-record-date buyer.

At 12% / 15% / 18% hurdles, central assumption-dependent entry prices are INR 116.07/101.70/89.42. These are not observable fair values. The linked growth×multiple grid and reverse hurdle enforce funding feasibility: no funded 15% crossing appears at 6x or 8x across 0–60% constant growth; at 10x, about 14.7% constant growth and INR 178.64 crore terminal annual sales suffice. Faster growth itself can exhaust cash. All value is realized through terminal ownership, so exit assumptions dominate. A 2% / 5% entry execution-cost sensitivity reduces central return to 8.56% / 7.93%; actual market impact may be larger. [S1,S5,S6,S11–S15]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The key thesis variable is realizable inventory cash, not nominal order demand. A lost decorator/customer or fashion shift can lower sales and margins while aged inventory and receivables persist. The adverse path combines 15% first-year revenue decline, 17% margin, 10% opening inventory writeoff and ONWC exceeding annual sales. It creates a modeled INR 11.09 crore funding deficit without rescue; its arithmetic terminal value is not an investable target. A 25% drop, 25% inventory impairment and no renewal of the revolver create a deficit of INR 41.16 crore. Neither is a forecast that the company has defaulted. A hypothetical later equity rescue at 80/share and 3% fees cannot cure cash becoming negative before the raise and is not called funded.

Even the funded adaptive-bear operating reset loses 66.06% of quoted entry value. The base itself is fragile: moving positive WC buildup evenly through the year rather than mainly into seasonal H2 creates a 1.60 crore gap; retaining opening WC intensity creates 14.50; an extra 5 crore completion bill creates 3.47. Minimum central monthly cash is only 1.42 crore. Excluding cash-in-hand leaves a 0.45 crore trough. Impairment is booked once against old stock, added back as noncash once, then replacement WC is funded once. Permanent-loss risk is High: dilution, distressed stock liquidation and trapped/inaccessible liquidity can damage common equity even while accounting profits stay positive. Counterevidence is strong actual revenue expansion, improving FY2026 CFO and reported current debt service. [S1,S4–S6,S11]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A five-year 5× price outcome requires about 38.0% annual appreciation and 10× requires 58.5%. The funded bull scenario reaches only about 2.78× the 133 entry price. Holding the base terminal EBIT margin, 8x EBIT multiple and net claims fixed merely for an arithmetic hurdle, 5× would require roughly INR 537 crore annual sales and 10× about INR 1,068 crore, well beyond management's broad 150–200 crore capability discussion. In reality the additional plant, WC, finance and dilution would change those claims and likely increase the burden. There is no verified capacity/customer/funding path supporting those outcomes today. Classification: speculative/unsupported, not a price target. [S1,S5,S6,S11]

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Research checkpoints, not automated trading rules: (1) Inventory INR 61.43 crore/March 2026: require conversion to sales/cash and independently clearer ageing; inventory/revenue failing to improve from 73.49% warns against the base efficiency assumption. (2) Average AR days 75.9 and 0.6866 crore over-one-year dues: watch a return above 90 days or rising old dues; simultaneous margin and collection deterioration breaks the cash thesis. (3) Cash INR 4.6351 crore and debt 56.3450: reconcile each half-year source/use bridge; a projected negative cash month without committed finance is a financing hold, while verified nonpayment is a distinct event. (4) Warrant deposit 6.95415 and unpaid 20.86245: track actual exercise before March 8, 2028 and match cash, shares, fees and objects; do not count an authorization as proceeds. (5) CWIP 29.8098 plus plant advances 8.1318: reconcile capitalization, completion spending and productive output; extra 5 crore cash requirements already breach the modeled cushion. (6) EBITDA margin 25.40% and FY2026 production 14.30% below target: distinguish utilization recovery from discount-led volume; two comparable weak half-years require a reset. (7) Franchise openings: baseline second Hyderabad outlet September 1; require dates, cohort sales and cash returns before crediting 10–15 new stores a year. (8) Clarify sanctioned-versus-drawn bank figures, RPT loan movements, utilization definitions and the historic compounding disposition; a corrected presentation is not automatically a thesis break, while substantiated adverse conduct is. (9) Liquidity: last trade October 13, lot 600; recheck live depth, lots and restrictions before any position decision. [S1,S4–S15]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Unrounded BQS 5.06 and IAS 3.415 place this in Weak setup / value-trap risk under the v3.0 matrix. The high raw sales factor does not offset weak cash realization; GQS remains 5.0 after the explicit cap. It is not an evidence-backed compounder candidate because business quality, moat, incremental returns, cash and balance resilience do not meet the required thresholds. Conditional action: research watchlist, not eligible as an attractive entry at this stale quote under the stated 15% hurdle. A cheaper price alone could improve R/P but would not repair CASH, CAP or funding. Actual normalized inventory conversion, a clear funded completion/renewal bridge and verified operating delivery are the main upgrades. Conversely, sustained cash absorption without committed funding would tighten G3; adverse substantiated integrity evidence would be assessed separately. No buy/sell order or user-specific allocation follows from this record. Rankings remain provisional within the researched universe and IAS is conditional on the October 13 quote and INR 5 lakh reference. [S1–S15]

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The source/evidence ledger distinguishes audited disclosure, calculations, management statements and analyst scenarios. Main audited statements and decisive debt/provision tables were inspected visually as well as textually. The complete signed prospectus was read from a public issuer-document mirror after two SEBI PDF transfers truncated; the SEBI index confirms the document. Original FY2021/FY2022 annual figures and IPO restatements, FY2023 original versus restated PAT, and FY2025 original versus later finance/CFO classifications are retained, not silently merged. The undated CSV snapshot was used only for discovery and never as current verified price or financial evidence.

Material open questions are the exact remaining plant completion commitments, accessible bank headroom/renewal terms, current SKU ageing and customer concentration, current RPT transaction reconciliation, and consistent capacity/utilization definitions. No later specific outcome was located for the historic MOA compounding item; the latest audit's broader no-material-litigation statement is the current available context. No independent credit-rating rationale was located, rather than asserting that a rating does not exist. A company may use certificates/guarantee approvals without those constituting cash facilities. The 0.0148 crore revenue-authority credit is excluded centrally because nature and legal offset/timing are unverified. Historical market data do not prove live execution. Base cash timing, WC improvement, capex and the terminal multiple are analyst assumptions explicitly stress-tested. These gaps reduce confidence and attractive-entry conviction without converting every supported factor to NS or accusing the issuer of wrongdoing. [S1–S21]

GOV.reason: Unmodified audit and disclosed proceeds/terms support an adequate baseline. Remuneration is 12.60% of group PAT, recurring procedural corrections and inconsistent RPT/facility tables constrain stewardship confidence. Counterpoint: no audited fraud/default finding, and personal guarantees support lenders rather than prove abuse.

MOAT.reason: Manufacturing and broad assortment improve response time versus imports; regional outlets aid access. Historic top five customers at 43.53% without long-term contracts and easy alternative decor sourcing limit switching barriers. No independently verified share or persistent premium establishes a strong structural moat.

REV.reason: Choose standalone FY2023–FY2026 CAGR 47.33% to avoid pandemic FY2021 and group-perimeter distortions; group CAGR is 49.8% and FY2026 group growth 41.95%. Raw band 9, capped at 8 for Medium driver confidence and three comparable post-pandemic intervals. No trajectory bonus or small-size penalty.

DUR.reason: Wedding/event demand, import substitution and regional franchising provide addressable avenues; a second Hyderabad opening is verified. However utilization definitions conflict, retail cohort economics are absent and funding-intensive assortment constrains practical access to the proposed runway.

CAP.reason: Committed funding capital rose sharply with CWIP/advances while the three-year incremental NOPAT/capital proxy is about 7.3%, below the 12–15% assumed nominal WACC. Current average capital return is around 12.8%. Counterpoint: much new capacity is immature, so this is not proof that every project destroys value; no separate persistent CAP cap applied.

CASH.reason: FY2024–2026 cumulative CFO is negative versus positive PAT; even correcting plant-advance classification leaves negative conversion. Inventory of INR 61.43 crore and long stock days dominate financing need. Counterpoint: FY2026 CFO turned positive and receivable days improved, but one year does not establish recovery from multi-year poor realization. Persistent CASH override applies.

BAL.reason: Debt of INR 56.35 crore versus cash of INR 4.64 crore and a large working-capital stock leave financing sensitivity. Base monthly cash stays positive only with renewal, seasonal receipt timing and efficiency gains; small timing/capex changes create gaps. Counterpoint: reported debt service is current and genuine warrant deposits arrived, without counting unreceived exercise cash.

EXEC.reason: Manufacturing production and new regional outlets demonstrate progress, and CFO became positive. Actual molding output was 14.30% below its FY2026 target, utilization disclosures are not on a reconciled basis, and earlier 10–20 retail-store ambitions lack a verified full opening cohort. Mixed delivery rather than automatic credit for announced capacity.

EARN.reason: PAT grew 13.09% and group operating EBITDA about 21% in FY2026, with other income a minority of profit. However revenue grew 41.95% and EBITDA margin fell from roughly 38% in FY2023 to 25.4%; forward cash interest on the larger debt base is materially above historical expensed interest. Bonus-adjusted FY2025/26 EPS of 8.56 / 9.68 is real but not extraordinary per-share compounding.

R.reason: Funded central case yields 8.991% annualized versus a 15% hurdle: spread of -6.009 percentage points, in the canonical -7 to less than -4 band. Base exit multiple of 8x EBIT is below the dated 12.25x bridge. Counterpoint: bull case exceeds hurdle, but requires better cash efficiency, margins and warrant exercise; not the base forecast.

D.reason: Even a funded adaptive bear ends near 45.14/share, about 66.06% below 133; no-reset bear and no-renewal severe paths have funding gaps and no investor IRR. Existing plant/inventory provide operating assets, but no independent liquidation valuation supports high recovery certainty.

P.reason: At 133, the central case misses 15%; its hurdle entry is about 101.70. A 10x EBIT exit plus 14.7% constant growth can meet 15%, but no funded crossing appears at 8x under the modeled financing rules. Recent rapid sales growth supports demand, yet cash timing and multiple normalization leave limited error tolerance.

L.reason: The 600-share lot is 79,800 at 133 and the conditional 60-session exit estimate is 102.28 days at 5% participation. Even observed-session-only exit is 26.97 days; last observed trade is October 13. Eligible SM and actual trading prevent a blanket suspension claim, but no orderly depth/spread evidence supports upgrading the bottom liquidity band.

Q.reason: Exact final BQS reused once, not rounded.

notes: Latest audited cash is March 2026. FY2027 is a forecast roll-forward including elapsed months, not reported monthly cash. H1 has an assumed 27% of revenue and 10% of annual positive WC absorption. A front-loaded WC sensitivity tests the timing dependence. All future capex and cash interest are funded separately.

Warrant deposits enter in September 2026. The 82% WC and 18% GCP pots are released only for qualifying WC absorption and operating costs. Exercise occurs only in explicitly labeled alternatives in March 2028, adding 1.554 million shares and INR20.86245 crore. No exercise is assumed centrally at an entry price below INR179.

No future discretionary dividends are assumed. The already-declared dividend leaves company cash in October 2026, but the record date precedes entry, so the new investor receives no dividend credit. Annualized return is measured from October 13, 2026 to October 13, 2031.
Opening inventory impairment reduces recoverable WC once and is a noncash PAT charge. Replacement target stock is funded from the adjusted opening balance. An impairment is not a cash release.

Opening current income tax is settled in June and September 2026; current gratuity in June; capital retention in December; related-party debt in FY2028. The unspecified revenue-authority balance is excluded centrally, with one separate recovery sensitivity. Noncurrent gratuity and deferred tax are retained terminal claims. Future ordinary benefit cash costs do not erase legacy benefits.

No incremental bank facility is presumed. Existing revolving borrowing renews centrally, with no-renewal stress. The hypothetical INR 20 crore recapitalization at INR 80 per share with 3% fees is uncommitted; it does not cure a prior cash deficit. No shareholder IRR is reported for an unfunded path.

Fixed deposits and operating deposits receive no free-cash credit. Completion cost, renewal and inventory realization remain uncertain. These are research-model assumptions, not findings that issuer accounts are misstated. Unfunded terminal values are arithmetic diagnostics only, not investable price targets.
